brief_bullets: Kolkata Police issue 11-point advisory; CM Adhikari hints at scrapping VIP entries at major pandals Among the 19 dead are 13 females, including two minors; the two other deceased minors are males Kolkata’s Bonedi Bari Durga pujas bring together grand colonial-era architecture, family legacies and heirloom recipes.

While the city’s pandals draw the biggest crowds, these ancestral homes offer a more intimate glimpse of the festival, following family traditions dating back more than 300 years Durga Puja celebrations mean glitzy pandals, excessive lighting, high-decibel music and many more attractions.But several committees organising the annual Durga Puja in Kokrajhar town in western Assam, the district headquarters of the Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR), have pitched in to adopt the concept of “carbon-neutral” celebrations by planting trees, reducing the use of non-biodegradable items and even lowering the volume of music systems to check sound pollution.A set of dos and don'ts were proposed by the Kokrajhar district administration for nearly 200 Durga Puja committees in the town as part of efforts to popularise the concept of “carbon-neutral” celebrations.“We proposed the idea as part of our efforts to have environmentally responsible festivities while preserving the religious and cultural essence of the festival.

It is very nice to see that nearly 50 per cent of the committees have responded very positively by significantly reducing the use of plastic items, planting trees and even controlling the volume of music systems,” Kokrajhar District Commissioner Pankaj Chakravarty told DH over the phone on Sunday.

Kokrajhar is situated about 200 km west of Guwahati.Durga Puja celebrations began on Friday and will continue till Wednesday, following which the Durga idols will be immersed in rivers.With a population of nearly 35,000 (2011 Census), Kokrajhar Municipal town has diverse communities, including Bodos, Bengalis, Assamese, Rabhas, Nepalis, Adivasis, Saranias and others, each peacefully celebrating their own festivals.Lotus theme, red-and-white decor to mark Durga Puja in BengaluruCarbon-neutral celebrationsUnder the concept of “carbon-neutral” celebrations, the district administration proposed several measures, such as encouraging the use of locally available and reusable materials, including bamboo, jute, recycled paper and other environmentally responsible alternatives, for pandals and decorations; promoting idols made from natural clay and other biodegradable materials, with non-toxic colours, to minimise environmental pollution, particularly during immersion; tree plantation; the use of solar energy and LED lights; responsible sound management; and encouraging waste segregation, responsible disposal and recycling, among other measures.“This is an encouraging beginning.
The drive is resulting in public awareness, with the concept being shared by many on social media platforms.
why_it_matters_bullets: Shifts federal policy priorities and legislative momentum ahead of upcoming electoral and administrative deadlines.

France wakes up to one of its worst bouts of unrest in years; one dead, 500 cops injured
France counts cost of worst unrest in years - ThePrint

brief_bullets: Paris: France woke on Sunday to the wreckage of one of its most violent days of unrest in years after protests over high prices and public services left one demonstrator dead, hundreds of police injured and nearly 1,800 people arrested.Nationwide demonstrations erupted into riots on Saturday, with a town hall torched, shops ransacked, and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country.One protester died after suffering a cardiac arrest during demonstrations in Paris, where police made a record 855 arrests.

Across France, police detained some 1,800 people and more than 500 officers were injured, the interior minister said.More than half a million people joined marches in scores of cities, marking the convergence of a month-long student movement with broader social discontent against rising living costs and declining public services.While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, looted luxury boutiques and supermarkets and attacked police vehicles and officers."No room for violence in our Republic," President Emmanuel Macron posted on X as the unrest unfolded late on Saturday. "Those who have ransacked, attacked the prefectures as well as businesses, looted even our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished."Aucune place pour la violence dans notre République.Ceux qui ont cassé, attaqué les préfectures comme les commerces, pillé jusqu’à nos mairies, seront poursuivis et punis.Aux forces de l’ordre, garantes du droit à manifester, je dis le soutien de la Nation.Nous ferons tous…— Emmanuel Macron (@EmmanuelMacron) October 17, 2026 A massive clean-up operation began in cities from Lille in the north to Marseille in the south and Strasbourg in the east to Bordeaux in the southwest, where a masked mob invaded the residence of the local prefect.Unrest mars day of violent protest in France, as student movement turns nationalIn Paris, smashed shop windows, burnt-out bicycles and spray-painted slogans bore witness to a day that began largely with peaceful demonstrations but descended into violence.In Limoges, workers assessed the damage to the 143-year-old city hall, which was partially destroyed in an arson attack.The unrest has increased pressure on Macron and his government.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the government would not be "intimidated" by violence, and blamed the unrest on the "ultra-left" and criminals, with a presidential election due next year.Economy Minister Roland Lescure pledged support for business owners who suffered losses. "Those who break things will pay, repair the damage and be held accountable for their intention to sow chaos," Lescure said in a statement.Bordeaux Mayor Thomas Cazenave said up to 100 stores had been looted in his city, while Marseille Mayor Benoit Payan announced emergency financial aid to support those businesses impacted by the violence.The protests began last month over school conditions and teacher shortages in working-class suburbs, before broadening into a movement against inequality, public spending cuts and the rising cost of living.
France counts cost of worst unrest in years ThePrint.

stories.primary_headline: Army officer’s wife booked in Jammu & Kashmir over alleged links with Chinese intelligence operatives

primary_source.headline: Army officer’s wife booked in Jammu & Kashmir over alleged links with Chinese intelligence operatives
primary_source.content: Srinagar: Jammu and Kashmir Police have booked the wife of a serving Army officer for alleged espionage-related activities involving foreign intelligence operatives, including those linked to China, with investigators examining research papers she allegedly prepared on sensitive defence and geopolitical issues.The woman, a freelance researcher from Telangana, has not been arrested, and a preliminary inquiry has not established that she shared sensitive information, official sources said on Sunday.The case was registered at Gandhi Nagar police station on Friday under the Official Secrets Act, 1923, and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).She was questioned by a Deputy Superintendent of Police-rank officer following the registration of the FIR, according to a PTI report.'Espionage Alert': UK accuses China of using academics to spy on AI and other tech researchInvestigators are examining allegations that the woman was tasked with preparing analytical papers on subjects including Line of Control (LoC) dynamics in Jammu and Kashmir, critical infrastructure projects in Arunachal Pradesh and drone deployment, sources said.The assignments allegedly involved individuals linked to Chinese intelligence operatives, they said.According to reports, the woman is well-qualified, undertook an IT internship with the United Nations in 2023 and currently works as a freelance researcher.The investigation is seeking to establish the nature of her contacts with foreign entities and whether any information or material was communicated to them.The allegations have not been independently established, and police have not publicly detailed the evidence recovered or confirmed whether any classified documents were involved.The investigation comes months after a Delhi court acquitted five accused in a separate espionage case registered in 2015.The accused, including serving and former security personnel, had faced charges under the Official Secrets Act over allegations of passing information about Army and Border Security Force deployments in Jammu and Kashmir to Pakistan-based intelligence operatives.In its May 20, 2026, judgment, the court found that the prosecution had failed to establish that the documents allegedly recovered were classified official records and that protected information had been communicated to enemy agents. All five accused were acquitted.

arrested, and a preliminary inquiry has not established that she shared sensitive information, official sources said on Sunday.The case was registered at Gandhi Nagar police station on Friday under the Official Secrets Act, 1923, and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).She was questioned by a Deputy Superintendent of Police-rank officer following the registration of the FIR, according to a PTI report.'Espionage Alert': UK accuses China of using academics to spy on AI and other tech researchInvestigators are examining allegations that the woman was tasked with preparing analytical papers on subjects including Line of Control (LoC) dynamics in Jammu and Kashmir, critical infrastructure projects in Arunachal Pradesh and drone deployment, sources said.The assignments allegedly involved individuals linked to Chinese intelligence operatives, they said.According to reports, the woman is well-qualified, undertook an IT internship with the United Nations in 2023 and currently works as a freelance researcher.The investigation is seeking to establish the nature of her contacts with foreign entities and whether any information or material was communicated to them.The allegations have not been independently established, and police have not publicly detailed the evidence recovered or confirmed whether any classified documents were involved.The investigation comes months after a Delhi court acquitted five accused in a separate espionage case registered in 2015.The accused, including serving and former security personnel, had faced charges under the Official Secrets Act over allegations of passing information about Army and Border Security Force deployments in Jammu and Kashmir to Pakistan-based intelligence operatives.In its May 20, 2026, judgment, the court found that the prosecution had failed to establish that the documents allegedly recovered were classified official records and that protected information had been communicated to enemy agents.
All five accused were acquitted.

primary_source.headline: Anti-CEC stir | Delhi Police registers cases, arrests 5 persons over attacks on protesters
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Delhi Police has registered at least 10 FIRs and arrested five people in connection with alleged harassment and assaults on protesters demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with several social media posts accusing right-wing activists of targeting demonstrators, officials said on Sunday.The cases were registered between October 11 and 14 at Connaught Place and Kamla Market police stations after videos and posts highlighting alleged attacks on protesters circulated on social media.At least five people have been arrested in two separate cases, a senior police officer said.According to the police, an FIR was registered at Connaught Place police station on October 13 in connection with an incident flagged through social media handles.Delhi Police registers four FIRs against 'rumour-mongers', Pak social media handles under scannerGaurav was arrested in the case, while efforts are underway to trace his alleged accomplices.A group of men was seen assaulting a protester while daring others to call them "cockroaches". One of the men was also heard threatening to beat up anyone who spoke against the prime minister or the police.In another case, registered at Kamla Market police station on October 11, four people were arrested after a video purportedly showing individuals harassing and assaulting protesters went viral.Police took suo motu cognisance of the incident and initiated legal action against those allegedly involved.The list of cases also includes multiple FIRs registered at Connaught Place police station on October 13 and 14 over incidents highlighted in social media posts and videos. Police are examining CCTV footage to identify those involved, establish the sequence of events and determine the roles of the suspected accused.EC-SIR row: Delhi Police take down 300 social media for spreading 'rumours'Several social media posts have alleged that right-wing activists assaulted or harassed protesters during the demonstrations.The footage and allegations are being examined by police as they work to identify the people involved and establish the circumstances surrounding the incidents.The police action comes amid a wider scrutiny of online content related to the protests, with authorities also investigating posts allegedly circulating misinformation, rumours and fabricated videos.Some social media accounts have shared claims of police brutality against demonstrators, which investigators are examining to establish their authenticity.In one of the cases, police have sought information from social media platform X to identify a user accused of uploading videos that they suspect were fabricated and circulated to disrupt public order.Police have identified more than 37 social media accounts, including over 17 allegedly linked to right-wing groups, for purportedly circulating misleading content related to the protests, a source in the police said.Takedown notices have been issued to more than 17 handles, including those linked to right-wing groups, and action has been initiated under relevant provisions of the Information Technology Act and other laws for allegedly inciting people and disrupting law and order, they said.Some right-wing accounts allegedly shared posts and reels targeting protesters and presenting the demonstrations in a misleading manner, while other users circulated videos purportedly showing police brutality against demonstrators.Investigators are examining the content to verify its authenticity and identify those responsible, the officials added.The protests in the national capital have been organised over demands for Kumar's resignation and a rollback of the SIR exercise. Further investigation in the cases is underway.

primary_source.content: India widens cancer drug price caps, lowering prices of 137 medicines  Reuters

sources.headline: India widens cancer drug price caps, lowering prices of 137 medicines - Reuters
Explained | Govt caps trade margins on 137 cancer drugs at 30%: NPPA
Government caps trade margins on 137 anti-cancer drugs at 30%

brief_bullets: The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers has announced a price cap of 30 per cent on the trade margins of 137 cancer medicines, over the cost of the drug at the first point, either to a stockist/distributor or the hospital.

These margins will apply when the drugs are sold directly to them by a manufacturer. The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), in an order dated October 17, has directed manufacturers to submit the revised MRP within seven days. "The revised prices shall come into effect from November 9," the gazette notification stated. Impact on cancer drug pricesAn analysis of pharmaceutical market data indicates that non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs carry an average trade mark-up of approximately 170 per cent, with mark-ups of up to 700 per cent in certain cases, according to an NPPA meeting conducted earlier.

This order is expected to reduce the MRP of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs by 70 per cent, depending on their current price structures. The 137 identified non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs include immunotherapy drugs used for treating over 20 types of cancers, denosumab used by breast and prostate cancer patients, pegfilgrastim, which is used to prevent neutropenia in cancer patients and bevacizumab, which is the approved drug to treat colon, ovarian, and cervical cancer.

With this notification, MRP of widely used anti-cancer drugs such as pembrolizumab, durvalumab and osimertinib is expected to become more accessible for cancer patients.Anti-cancer drug prices to come down as govt caps trade margins at 30%Centre caps trade margins on cancer medicines at 30% of MRPMarket overview: scheduled vs non-scheduled drugsCurrently, the anti-cancer drugs market comprises nearly 225 drugs and 500 formulations, with an annual turnover of around Rs 12,500 crore.

Of this, scheduled cancer drugs that come under price control account for approximately Rs 2,250 crore, with the balance comprising non-scheduled drugs.To ensure that these life-saving medicines remain available, manufacturers of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs will be required to maintain their current production levels.
why_it_matters_bullets: Marks an important milestone in treatment development, shaping clinical guidelines and patient standard-of-care.

stories.primary_headline: One month of IIT Bombay student's death: No arrests yet; protest continues

primary_source.headline: One month of IIT Bombay student's death: No arrests yet; protest continues
primary_source.content: Mumbai: Exactly a month after Sahil Wakode, a student of Indian Institute of Technology-Bombay died by suicide, students and activists staged a protest outside the institute’s Powai campus on Sunday, however, police dispersed the mob and detained several of them.The parents of Sahil—Ravindra Wakode and Sonali Wakode—too were part of the protests.&nbsp;On 18 September, Sahil (20), a second-year student from Energy Science and Engineering Department, was caught allegedly using a mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid-semester examination. However, his body was later found in his hostel room.&nbsp;The case is being investigated by the&nbsp;Crime Branch-CID, which has taken over investigations from the Powai police station.&nbsp;Sahil Wakode death: Protesting IIT Bombay students claim detention, use of excessive force by policeThe parents are demanding action and arrest of&nbsp; Prof Shireesh Kedare, the Director of&nbsp; Indian Institute of Technology-Bombay and Prof Suryanarayana Doolla, a faculty member of the premier institute’s Energy Science and Engineering Department.Meanwhile, the Congress once again backed the parents and said that it will ensure that Sahil Wakode gets justice. Sahil Wakode, a backward-class student at the IIT Mumbai institution, did not commit suicide; it was "an institutional murder."“Even though a month has passed since this incident, no action has been taken against anyone yet. In the past 13 months, 4 students in this institution have died by suicide. After Sahil's death, students in the institution are protesting, and the police are committing atrocities against them, beating them. On whose orders are the police committing atrocities in the institution's premises? All these things must stop. An inquiry must be conducted quickly, and strict action must be taken against those responsible for Sahil's murder,” said Mumbai Congress president and MP Prof Varsha Gaikwad.&nbsp;“RSS ideology has infiltrated this prestigious IIT institution, and this is not good for the education sector. Keep educational institutions away from political ideologies,” she added.&nbsp;A delegation from the All India Independent Scheduled Castes Association arrived at the IIT Bombay gates around noon, seeking to pay respects to Sahil.&nbsp;

primary_source.headline: Gómez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton’s 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal Palace
primary_source.content: At last, Fabian Hürzeler has the scalp that matters most to all Brighton fans and in humiliating fashion. Diego Gómez’s breathtaking goal-of-the-season contender from the halfway line, à la David Beckham, was the highlight of another hugely impressive performance from the Premier League’s top scorers as they continued their flying start to the season.Not since a 4-1 thrashing here in February 2024 under Roberto De Zerbi had Brighton tasted victory against their arch rivals from up the A23 – a run of four matches. But having been handed the initiative by Jaydee Canvot’s own goal, a stunned Palace found themselves 3-0 down after 10 minutes. It got even worse for Pierre Sage after Brighton extended their lead through Gómez’s wonderstrike and Yasin Ayari, with Charalampos Kostoulas adding a fourth after half-time and the substitute Jack Hinshelwood’s late header matching their record 5-0 win over Palace from 1956 in Division Three South. sources.headline: Aamir Khan meets Raj Thackeray amid nephew Imran’s legal challenge to leave India notice
Aamir Khan meets Raj Thackeray amid nephew Imran's exit notice row

brief_bullets: Mumbai: Actor-filmmaker Aamir Khan met Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) president Raj Thackeray at his residence in Mumbai on Sunday.The details of the meeting were not immediately known.The meeting comes days after Aamir Khan's nephew and actor Imran Khan was served a notice by the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer (FRRO), directing him to leave India by October 28.

Imran had reportedly participated in the October 10 protests at August Kranti Maidan in Mumbai, demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process.The 43-year-old Imran Khan is a US citizen and an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder.'Leave India': Imran Khan moves Bombay HC against 'illegal, bad in law' notice by Mumbai police, FRRO issues him show-cause noticeHe has challenged the notice in the Bombay High Court, which is expected to hear the matter this week.

The plea is expected to be mentioned for an urgent hearing before a division bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna.“The notice has been issued without disclosing any reasons, supporting material, or specific statutory contravention.

It was issued without inquiry, a show-cause notice, or any opportunity for the Petitioner (Khan) to respond to the alleged violations,” the plea stated.The FRRO issued the notice under Sections 7 and 29 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, directing Imran Khan to leave India by October 28, 2026.
why_it_matters_bullets: Shifts federal policy priorities and legislative momentum ahead of upcoming electoral and administrative deadlines.

The CJP leaders maintained that they had unfurled the national flag and raised slogans.In a post on X, Singh said she had been at the police station since 11 am, while the hearing was scheduled for noon.

She said the Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP/SEM) had not arrived at the Mandir Marg police station by 4.42 pm.CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde under preventive arrest; likely to be produced before magistrate"This is really concerning.
They have rejected 4 sureties till now on vague reasons.

stories.primary_headline: Tilak Varma relishes new role as finisher

primary_source.headline: Tilak Varma relishes new role as finisher
primary_source.content: Bengaluru: India’s T20I vice-captain Tilak Varma has never shied away from talking his heart out. And for someone who loves pace on the ball and batting at No. 3, dropping down to No. 5 or even No. 6 is not an ideal situation to be in.However, for Tilak, who rarely gets to bat in his preferred position in a changed set-up, versatility has been his biggest strength.&nbsp;Asian Games 2026 | Abhishek Sharma, Tilak Varma do the star turn as India beat Pakistan by 19 runs to defend titleFrom the third T20I against South Africa in Dharamsala in December 2025 to the T20 World Cup (Super Eights vs South Africa) in Ahmedabad in February, Tilak regularly batted at No. 3 for seven straight games.And since his debut, if not on some rare occasion, Tilak has been a standard in India’s T20 top-four. Once Sanju Samson returned to the XI to accompany Abhishek Sharma at the top, and with Ishan Kishan playing one drop, Tilak was pushed down the order as a floating option. He admits that the situation is “unfortunate”, but India’s vice-captain also understands what it means to be a team-player, while enjoying the role of a finisher. “It is not easy to change the numbers (batting) from No. 3 to No. 5 and No. 6. It will be slightly challenging. But I have been working on that, especially how to finish the games. I have said I love finishing the games for India,” Tilak said after the series-deciding fifth T20I was called off due to persistent rain.For me as an individual, if you see, it will be easier batting at 3. But unfortunately, I should bat at 5 or 6 because we have got that combination at the top right now. Kishan (Ishan) is batting at 3, and he is doing brilliantly. I think there is no option but to bat at five or six and do the job."Talking about his role clarity and preparation in his transition to a T20I finisher, Tilak highlighted he’s got all the shots in the book and is confident of changing positions with just a few sessions in the nets. And the numbers are impressive: averaging 65.66 in nine games.“We should do that (working on his skills as a finisher), otherwise, it will be tough. When you go in to bat as a finisher, if the ball comes in your arc, you should try to hit it for a six. Because, if you see in T20s, most of the time in this role, you get to bat a maximum of five or six overs.“If you see, I have been in this role in my childhood as well. I have got shots all over the ground. So I am confident that whether I bat at three or five, I have got the technique to adapt, and if I practice for a day or two, I can do any role for the team. Now even if I come back to No. 3, I can adapt within a day or two of practice. I am confident of batting anywhere,” he said.

stories.primary_headline: Delhi: Class 12 student stabbed to death outside school, five apprehended

primary_source.headline: Delhi: Class 12 student stabbed to death outside school, five apprehended
primary_source.content: New Delhi: A 17-year-old Class 12 student was allegedly stabbed to death outside a government school in southwest Delhi's Mohan Garden area following an altercation between two students over the prescribed school shoes, police said on Sunday.Five accused, including three minors and two adults, have been apprehended in connection with the murder, three of whom are students of the same school, they said.The incident took place on October 14 when a PCR call regarding a stabbing incident near a government school in Mohan Garden was received at 6.10 pm at the local police station. The victim, a resident of Mohan Garden, had sustained stab injuries and was taken to Tarak Hospital, where he succumbed during treatment, the police said.Class 11 student fatally stabbed in south Delhi; two heldAccording to an eyewitness, a Class 12 student of the same school, the dispute began after another student complained to a teacher that he was not wearing the prescribed school-pattern shoes. This led to a heated argument between the two, during which the latter allegedly threatened him.After school hours, when the student left the premises with his friends, including the victim, the other student allegedly instigated the remaining accused, following which the group assaulted them. During the attack, one of the assailants allegedly stabbed the victim, causing fatal injuries, the police said.The knife allegedly used in the crime was recovered near the school gate.The victim's father is an ex-serviceman and is currently employed as a gunman in Gurugram, police said.

stories.primary_headline: The Guardian view on plague in Russia: what is most worrying is the lack of information | Editorial

primary_source.headline: The Guardian view on plague in Russia: what is most worrying is the lack of information | Editorial
primary_source.content: In the three weeks since a health worker’s death in Siberia, officials have stonewalled the WHO – setting a worrying precedent for future pandemicsIs there a plague outbreak in Russia? If the answer were a clear yes, there shouldn’t be much reason to worry. With swift medical intervention, plague is treatable. But in the nearly three weeks since a worker at a Siberian plague research unit died of a mysterious respiratory illness, state officials have been consistently tight-lipped about what happened and whether there were any further cases.It is this uncertainty that has the World Health Organization (WHO) and international community worried: partly because there is a – very small – risk of an outbreak, and partly because it is yet another warning that the international coordination we rely on to prevent pandemics is fraying along with the rest of international politics, and could easily fail to protect us in the future. stories.primary_headline: They came to see Kolkata's famous pandals, but never returned home

primary_source.headline: They came to see Kolkata's famous pandals, but never returned home
primary_source.content: Kolkata: Pranjal Sarkar had no visible injuries anywhere else on his body. The only mark was that of a shoe on the left side of his face, a grim imprint of the brutal force of the footstep of an unknown person who may have unwittingly crushed the 13-year-old to death when the crowd surged at the Durga Puja pandal in Chorbagan in north-central Kolkata.Pranjal watched videos of the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samiti’s pandal on social media. The 13-year-old might not have fully grasped the “Beyond Sound” theme conceived and brought to life by artist Susanta Shibani Paul, but the sight of Goddess Durga and her four children, Kartik, Ganesh, Lakshmi and Saraswati, seated on a crescent moon amid dim, celestial lighting, caught his imagination. He insisted that the pandal be a must-see when his parents, Anukul Sarkar and Priyanka Sarkar, brought him from Agarpara in the North 24 Parganas district to Kolkata on the second day of the autumn festival.Little did Pranjal or his parents know that a danger lurked beneath the pandal’s surreal ambience, one that would turn the family’s Durga Puja outing into an unimaginable tragedy.The boy was one of the 19 people killed in the stampede at the pandal on Saturday. His parents survived, though. “He would have left for a tour to Shillong today with my sister and brother-in-law. Instead, I had to see the lifeless body of my nephew,” Pranjal’s maternal uncle said in front of the mortuary of Kolkata Medical College and Hospital on Sunday. “My brother-in-law could save seven or eight other children, but not his own son.”Even as the autumn festival unfolded across West Bengal, the stampede cast a pall of gloom over the families of the deceased and their neighbourhoods, from Kolkata and the Hooghly, Purba Bardhaman, North 24 Parganas and Nadia districts of West Bengal to Muzaffarpur in Bihar, turning what should have been a time of celebration into one of mourning.Kolkata stampede: Families mourn loss of loved ones as evening of festivity turned into heartacheSriparna Poddar, a 27-year-old nurse at a hospital in Kolkata, was often the first person her neighbours in Baidyabati, Hooghly, approached for healthcare advice. But on Sunday, she lay dead among the other victims of the stampede, while her family and neighbours waited to take home her mortal remains.Sandeep Bej, another 13-year-old boy, wanted to stay in his village in Madhabdihi in Purba Bardhaman for the Durga Puja celebrations but, at the last moment, went to Kolkata with his mother, Tagar Bej, 37, to see some of the city's pandals. However, the mother-son duo died in the stampede. So did Tagar’s sister, Piyali. Sandeep’s sister, Agamani Bej, was injured. “They were expected to return to their village on Sunday. But now only their mortal remains will return.”Ram Biswas came from Chakdaha in Nadia with his wife, Arati Sarkar Biswas, for pandal-hopping in Kolkata. He survived the stampede at Chorbagan but could not save his wife. Recalling the horror, Ram said that the crowd surged into the pandal after the ropes restricting entry were removed when it started raining. “It was dark inside, and people rushing in knocked others to the ground. Arati and I fell. I somehow got up and tried to pull her to her feet, but I couldn’t. My wife died before my eyes. I could do nothing,” Ram said on Sunday.For Abhishek Srivastava and his 13-year-old son, Ayansh, the trip to Kolkata was meant to be their first experience of the city’s famed Durga Puja celebrations. The two travelled from Muzaffarpur in Bihar to visit relatives in Agarpara, West Bengal, and went pandal-hopping with family members on Saturday. But both died in the stampede.Tania Biswas and Barnali Haldar, both 17, had planned their Maha Saptami outing well in advance. The Class XI students from Gouranga Nagar in New Town were close friends who had decided to wear sarees for the occasion. They set out with five other friends to visit the city’s Durga Puja pandals, but the outing ended in tragedy in Chorbagan, where both died in the stampede.Barnali’s father, Binod Haldar, who ekes out a living by pulling a rickshaw around New Town, learnt of his daughter’s death while he was still working. Her friends called him, and he rushed to the hospital, only to find that his elder child had already died. He spent the night outside the hospital mortuary. “My world has ended,” he said in a trembling voice, with tears rolling down his cheeks. “There will never be a Durga Puja in our lives again.”

The 13-year-old might not have fully grasped the “Beyond Sound” theme conceived and brought to life by artist Susanta Shibani Paul, but the sight of Goddess Durga and her four children, Kartik, Ganesh, Lakshmi and Saraswati, seated on a crescent moon amid dim, celestial lighting, caught his imagination. stories.primary_headline: FSSAI urges safe transport and storage of perishable foods to prevent spoilage

primary_source.headline: FSSAI urges safe transport and storage of perishable foods to prevent spoilage
primary_source.content:
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has directed all food business operators to ensure that perishable food items like khoa, paneer, meat, and fish are transported safely in hygienic conditions.&nbsp;“Owing to their perishable nature, these food items are highly susceptible to microbial growth and spoilage if not maintained under appropriate temperature conditions,” the FSSAI advisory dated October 15 stated.&nbsp;In the advisory, the food regulatory authority revealed that perishable food items like khoa, paneer, meat, etc are not handled, stored, or transported under appropriate temperature conditions. This should be maintained throughout the supply chain, from procurement till delivery to the end consumer. Subjecting these food items to temperature abuse may adversely affect food safety and public health and constitutes non-compliance with the hygiene and sanitary requirements prescribed by the FSSAI.&nbsp;FSSAI issues an advisory on handling, storage, and transportation of perishable foods like khoas, paneer, meat, and fish under controlled temperature conditions throughout the supply chain.  
FBOs must ensure strict adherence to hygiene and temperature standards 
#FSSAIAdvisory https://t.co/U4XZc09Xf4&mdash; FSSAI (@fssaiindia) October 18, 2026
 FSSAI proposes banning addition of fructose, sucrose in baby food productsFSSAI proposes stricter front-of-pack warning label rules for packaged foods after backlashThe regulator further added that FBOs should use only food-grade packaging materials and suitable secondary packaging. The use of gunny bags or other non-food-grade coverings for packing or transporting compromises product safety and should be avoided.&nbsp;Additionally, food businesses should also ensure that necessary measures are taken to protect products from dust, moisture, pests, physical damage and cross-contamination during storage, loading, unloading and transportation.&nbsp;They must also maintain proper records and traceability of consignments and produce invoices or other relevant documents whenever demanded by the competent authority.

stories.primary_headline: ‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva laid to rest amid tears, tributes

primary_source.headline: ‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva laid to rest amid tears, tributes
primary_source.content: Ranipet (Tamil Nadu): Veteran Tamil music composer and singer Deva, popularly known as 'Thenisai Thendral', was laid to rest with full state honours at his family farmland in Sakkaramallur near Arcot, Ranipet district, on Sunday.He was 75.Deva died of a heart attack in Chennai on the morning of October 17.His mortal remains were taken from his Chennai residence to the farmland, where the final rites were performed.Thousands of people gathered at the site to pay their last respects to the celebrated music director.Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay had visited Deva's residence in Chennai to pay his respects and announced that the funeral would be held with state honours in recognition of the composer's contribution to the music industry.Revenue and police officials oversaw arrangements for the ceremony at Sakkaramallur.‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva (1950-2026): The maestro who took gaana to the masses Relatives and villagers recalled Deva's enduring connection to his roots, saying he regularly visited his native village during festivals such as Pongal and contributed to local initiatives, including funding the construction of a Sri Ranganathar temple.Born Devanesan Chokkalingam, Deva had a career spanning nearly four decades and composed music for more than 400 films in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam.Before turning to films, Deva was an employee of the Tamil Nadu government’s Public Works Department (PWD).He made his entry as a composer in 1986 with 'Mattukkara Mannaru', which did not fare well in theatres, though its songs found a loyal audience over time.'Manasukketha Maharasa' (1989), starring Ramarajan and Seetha, was the film that first drew attention to his work. His real breakthrough, however, came in 1990 with the Prashanth-starrer 'Vaigasi Poranthachu', which won him widespread acclaim.Deva rose to prominence in the late 1980s and 1990s with his high-energy, folk-rooted tunes, and is widely credited with bringing the ‘gaana’ genre into mainstream Tamil cinema.Few composers in Tamil cinema are as closely identified with one genre as Deva is with 'gaana', the urban folk music born in the working-class neighbourhoods of North Chennai.He worked with nearly every leading star of his time, among them Vijayakanth, Sarathkumar, Vijay and Ajith, and delivered some of the biggest hits of their careers.Among his chartbusters were the Rajinikanth films ‘Annamalai’, ‘Baashha’ and ‘Arunachalam’, and the Kamal Haasan outings ‘Avvai Shanmugi’, ‘Pammal K Sambandam’ and ‘Panchathanthiram’.His death drew tributes from political leaders, members of the film fraternity and fans across Tamil Nadu.

primary_source.headline: The problem with telling people the world is ending
primary_source.content: In the face of terrible crises, it can feel right to shock people into action. But what if that has the opposite effect?These days, it’s easy to succumb to hopelessness. Whether you’re thinking about the climate crisis, the prospect of AI apocalypse, war or political turmoil, the list of challenges facing humanity can seem insurmountable.It certainly feels unprecedented, and much of it may be. The sense of impending doom, on the other hand, is nothing new. And what we have learned from the past is that doomerism can lead to paralysis. If everyone freezes, then nothing changes – but if we want to have a chance of mitigating some of the threats I’ve mentioned then action is what’s required. Continue reading...

primary_source.content: Facing a slump in the polls, Argentina’s president is making economic attacks on the islands’ oil industry, and suggesting its key fisheries industry could be next A dozen local people and a uniformed military police officer (“Do you mind if I sit in?”) took their seats at the back of the handsome wood-panelled courtroom that doubles as the Falkland Islands’ legislative assembly. Outside, it was a typically blowy early evening. It may nominally be spring in the south Atlantic, but Stanley harbour, with its dark grey water speckled with historical shipwrecks, was a cauldron of swells and churn.Six of the assembly’s eight members – five men, one woman – waited patiently at a row of desks and microphones. The heating had been turned up to just short of uncomfortable. Behind them, a portrait of King Charles. From the other walls, dusty photographs of governors peered down on the scene. stories.primary_headline: Reports of sale false and misleading, says Bhilai Steel Plant amid Congress alleging Adani visit

primary_source.headline: Reports of sale false and misleading, says Bhilai Steel Plant amid Congress alleging Adani visit
primary_source.content: Durg: Bhilai Steel Plant (BSP), a Chhattisgarh-based unit of state-run Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), on Sunday dismissed reports about its proposed sale as "false and misleading", the assertion coming amid allegations from the Congress that the Adani Group was planning to visit the facility.The BSP is located in Bhilai city in Durg district.In a statement, the BSP said the Ministry of Steel has refuted the claims through its official social media handle, while the Press Information Bureau (PIB) Fact Check had also confirmed that the reports are false.The plant appealed to its employees, stakeholders and the people of Chhattisgarh not to believe or circulate unverified information and urged them to rely on official and authenticated sources."BSP is not merely an industrial establishment; it is an integral part of Chhattisgarh's identity, pride and industrial legacy. Since its inception, the plant has played a pivotal role in the state's industrial development by generating employment, supporting ancillary industries and contributing to the livelihoods of thousands of families," it said.Its legacy and contribution have made it a source of pride for the people of Chhattisgarh, the statement asserted.Karnataka government to negotiate with Adani over tunnel road costAs a major unit of SAIL, the Bhilai Steel Plant continues to contribute to the growth of the country's steel sector and strengthen India's industrial capabilities, the statement said.The BSP urged the people to refrain from spreading misinformation that could create unnecessary confusion among employees, their families and the people of Chhattisgarh.The clarification came after former Chhattisgarh chief minister and senior Congress leader Bhupesh Baghel alleged that Adani was likely to visit the plant.In a post on X on October 14, Baghel said, "It has come to light that Adani is set to visit the Bhilai Steel Plant - our BSP. Do you understand the implications of Adani's visit to the BSP? It means that Narendra Modi who is spearheading a campaign to sell off the nation, has now set his sights on our BSP. And his favored buyer is coming to conduct an inspection"."Modi ji should realize that the BSP is the soul of Chhattisgarh. And we, the people of Chhattisgarh, will not allow it to be sold under any circumstances. Not under any circumstances," Baghel added.Chhattisgarh BJP leaders should also understand that BSP is not for sale, Baghel had said.Meanwhile, Congress's Bhilai unit president Mukesh Chandrakar, in a statement on Sunday, said reports about the plant's possible privatisation and the Adani Group's alleged visit had triggered anger in the industrial town.The reports had created apprehensions among employees, local shopkeepers and residents over job security, minimum wages for workers and the future of the plant's township, he claimed.

When Lokesh reached the spot, he allegedly witnessed Ajith attacking Uday with a knife. When Lokesh attempted to intervene, the accused allegedly chased him. primary_source.content: It’s a perfect storm of protesters with heartfelt grievances and others set on conflict. The key here is the sense of betrayal that united them on the streetsThe first thing I learned on the streets of Paris this weekend is that there is no arguing with teargas. I arrived at Place de la République just after 1pm yesterday. The mood was festive until police started firing volleys of teargas into the square from Rue du Faubourg-du-Temple.I didn’t see the inciting incident – if there even was one – and tried walking into the cloud of CS gas hanging in the air. It was impossible. The gas clings to your nose and burns your eyes, and you quickly start struggling to breathe. I retreated towards the Boulevard de Magenta, blinking furiously to stop the stinging.Oliver Haynes is a journalist and co-host of Sacré Bleu: the French presidential election podcastDo you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? stories.primary_headline: Private complaints over false election affidavits need no official sanction: Supreme Court

primary_source.headline: Private complaints over false election affidavits need no official sanction: Supreme Court
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Private citizens can file criminal complaints against candidates for submitting false affidavits with their nomination papers, the Supreme Court has ruled, clarifying that no prior sanction or complaint from the Election Commission or any public servant is required.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu held that an offence under Section 125-A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, does not fall within the restrictive ambit of Section 195 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. EC-SIR row | ‘Undermining EC, Supreme Court is not a right’: Harvard scholars warns against erosion of public trust in IndiaThe non-obstante clause in Section 125-A and the deliberate legislative omission to include it in Section 195 CrPC mean courts can take cognizance of such complaints lodged by private persons under Section 200 CrPC, the court said.The ruling came in an appeal filed by Rajkumar Madki challenging a March 7, 2025, judgment of the Karnataka High Court. The High Court had quashed Madki’s August 2023 private complaint against Dr Shailendra Beldale, the MLA from Bidar, alleging that the legislator had given a false residential address in the affidavit accompanying his 2023 nomination papers.The October 16, 2026 decision settles a substantial question of law of general public importance that had not been previously decided by the court.The High Court had held that only the Election Commission could complain of an offence under Section 125-A and that a voter’s remedy was limited to an election petition. The Supreme Court disagreed on the legal point, observing that courts cannot expand the list of offences requiring a public servant’s complaint by implication.“The prohibition on a court taking cognizance… is restricted to the offences specifically enumerated therein,” the bench said. Supreme Court seeks replies from CEC Gyanesh Kumar, others on plea filed by Rahul Gandhi, oppn leadersIt noted that Section 125-A is of relatively recent origin and that Parliament could have amended Section 195 CrPC if it intended to restrict such prosecutions. Guidelines or press notes issued by the Election Commission, the court added, cannot bind judicial interpretation of the statute.Despite upholding the maintainability of private complaints in principle, the apex court declined to revive the specific case against Beldale, represented by senior advocate Anand Sanjay M Nuli. It found that the documents on record effectively rebutted the allegation of false declaration of residence and that the prospect of conviction was remote. Continuing the trial, the court said, would only waste judicial time.The High Court’s order quashing the proceedings was therefore left undisturbed, but on different grounds. The Supreme Court made it clear that magistrates retain full powers to deal with frivolous or harassing complaints if any are filed in future.

stories.primary_headline: Zubeen Garg murder case: Assam CID to challenge bail for bandmate, cousin in SC

primary_source.headline: Zubeen Garg murder case: Assam CID to challenge bail for bandmate, cousin in SC
primary_source.content: Guwahati: Amid sharp public reactions to the bail granted to two accused in the alleged murder case of Zubeen Garg, the Assam CID on Sunday said it had decided to challenge the bail orders in the Supreme Court.Special Director General of Police, CID, Munna Prasad Gupta said the decision to move the Supreme Court challenging the bail granted by the Gauhati High Court to two accused, female bandmate Amritprabha Mahanta and cousin Sandipan Garg, was taken after examining the bail orders.Mahanta was granted bail on October 9, while Garg, a suspended Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP), got bail from the High Court on Friday. Both were present when cultural icon Zubeen Garg died at sea in Singapore on September 19 last year. Garg drowned during a yacht party.Assam Advocate General Devajit Saikia told reporters that the decision to challenge the bail orders was taken after loopholes were detected in the High Court orders granting bail to Amritprabha and Sandipan.Two of Zubeen's personal security officers (PSOs) were also granted bail by the High Court earlier.Following the bail orders, many expressed doubts over Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma's claim that Garg was murdered by the accused and his assurance of justice.Zubeen Garg death case: After bandmate, cousin Sandipan gets bailThe influential All Assam Students' Union even demanded that the state government challenge the bail orders in the Supreme Court.The three remaining accused, Shyamkanu Mahanta, Garg's manager Siddharth Sharma, and Shekhar Jyoti Goswami, a drummer in Garg's band, are still in judicial custody. Garg was in Singapore to attend the Northeast India Festival organised by Shyamkanu Mahanta's firm.The trial in the case, however, is underway in a fast-track court.Although Garg's death was initially suspected to be a drowning mishap, CM Sarma claimed that he was murdered by a few people and that others had assisted them.Sarma even told the Assembly that it was a "plain and simple murder case". A coroner's court in Singapore, however, ruled in March this year that Garg's death was due to drowning and that no foul play could be established.Lakhs of his fans, who were emotional and angry, took to the streets and demanded exemplary punishment for those responsible for the alleged crime.

stories.primary_headline: Mysuru Dasara: Final round of rehearsal begins for all 13 Dasara elephants

primary_source.headline: Mysuru Dasara: Final round of rehearsal begins for all 13 Dasara elephants
primary_source.content: Mysuru: After 48 days of training, the final round of the last two days' of rehearsal began for all 13 Dasara Elephants infront of Mysuru Palace on Sunday morning.&nbsp;Flanked by Cauvery and Roopa, lead Elephant Prashantha, who has been finalised for carrying golden howdah, marched towards the podium.&nbsp;Chief Conservator of Forest Mysuru circle S S Ravishankar, DCF, Wildlife&nbsp;I B Prabhugowda, Mysuru city police commissioner Seema Latkar offered floral benediction as part of the rehearsal. On Wednesday Chief Minister D K Shivakumar will offer floral benediction to the idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari which will be housed in golden howdah, mounted on Prashantha at the end of Dasara Jamboo Savari procession on Vijayadashami on October 21. This year, even Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Kerala who are expected to participate in the procession, are also likely to accompany CM D K Shivakumar on the podium, according to sources.Mysuru Dasara: 'Prashantha' to be lead elephant carrying golden howdah in Vijayadashami processionThe Police band led by band master B Manjunath, played even the national song-Vande Matharam for the first time along with the national Anthem during the floral benediction. Mounted cops&nbsp;also joined the rehearsal.&nbsp;Parade commander K N Suresh, Assistant Parade commander&nbsp;Sharanappa Sasanur&nbsp;accompanied the howdah Elephant.&nbsp;Prior to that, Abhimanyu marched as the&nbsp;Nishaane Elephant leading the procession at the forefront. Gopi followed him as the Nauphath Elephant. Mahendra and Lakshmi; Srirama, Chithra and Sugreeva; Srikanta and Ekalavya marched as Saalanes in three batches.&nbsp;Veteran Abhimanyu who carried golden howdah for six years till last year, has been relieved from this prime duty this year as he has turned 60 years of age. Hence Prashantha, Mahendra, Dhananjaya, Ekalavya and Sugreeva were trained to carry the weight equivalent to golden howdah. After the completion of their training on Tuesday, Prashantha was finalised on Wednesday to carry golden howdah in the procession.&nbsp;Dasara elephants, horses acquainted with cannon fire shotsThe first batch of nine Dasara elephants arrived at the Aranya Bhavan in Mysuru after a grand Gajapayana event at Veeranahosahalli in Hunsur taluk on August 26. They were accorded a grand traditional welcome on the Palace premises on August 28 and have been housed there since then. Their weight was checked, and they are being treated to a special nutritious diet to maintain their strength and build stamina for the big day, from August 30. Their training began on August 30. They were familiarised with the crowd, and the procession route from Palace to Government Ayurveda college circle till September 4. From September 5, they were familiarised with the entire procession route till Bannimantap ground. Training to carry weight began on September 6. Elephants Sugreeva, Roopa and Chaithra arrived in the second batch on September 13. Training to carry wooden howdah began on September 25. They were acquainted with cannon fire shots from brass barrels on October 7, 9 and 12, as 21 Cannon shots will be fired during floral benediction to Goddess at the end of procession on Vijayadashami.&nbsp;

stories.primary_headline: EC-SIR row | Congress says nothing can save Gyanesh Kumar, seeks major revamp of the poll body

primary_source.headline: EC-SIR row | Congress says nothing can save Gyanesh Kumar, seeks major revamp of the poll body
primary_source.content:
New Delhi: As the Election Commission "resumes" distribution of "readable" electoral rolls to parties after a "gap of eight years", Congress on Sunday said "nothing can save" Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar while insisting that a "thorough" revamp of the poll body and its IT system is required.General Secretary (Communications) Jairam Ramesh said the decision to provide electoral rolls in readable PDF format  was the result of the whole nation being on the streets against the "vote chors".EC-SIR row | People's Movement march seeking Gyanesh Kumar's removal on October 23The attack comes as the Congress prepares to host I.N.D.I.A. bloc parties at a rally in Ramlila Maidan on November 1 against the CEC.In a post on 'X', he said over the past two years, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and the Congress have been "persistent, insistent and consistent" in demanding that the EC provide electoral rolls in searchable format to all parties. पिछले दो वर्षों से लोकसभा में विपक्ष के नेता श्री राहुल गांधी और कांग्रेस पार्टी लगातार, मजबूती से और पुरजोर तरीके से यह मांग करते आ रहे हैं कि भारत निर्वाचन आयोग सभी राजनीतिक दलों को मतदाता सूची ऐसे डिजिटल फॉर्मेट में उपलब्ध कराए, जिसमें मतदाताओं के नाम और अन्य जानकारी आसानी से…&mdash; Jairam Ramesh (@Jairam_Ramesh) October 18, 2026
 

"The demand was repeatedly refused by the ECI - which stopped providing searchable voter rolls in 2018 when the Congress found lakhs of bogus voters in Madhya Pradesh. The demand was denied for eight years to enable 'vote chori'," he claimed.Referring to the October 15 announcement by the EC on providing voter lists in readable format, he said "every time Vote Chori is caught, the Modi government adopts a new tactic: stopping readable voter rolls, fake voter additions, SIR. But not this time.""Nothing can save the CEC Gyanesh Kumar who, acting on the instructions of the PM and the HM, has destroyed public trust and confidence in the ECI. He simply has to go. But that alone will not be enough. The ECI itself along with its IT system has to be thoroughly revamped," he said. TThe SIR, that has put the Constitutional right to vote for over 13 crore Indians at risk, has to be suspended forthwith, he added.

stories.primary_headline: Huge sand deposits remain utilised in Keralam even as state laments over Tamil Nadu's restriction

primary_source.headline: Huge sand deposits remain utilised in Keralam even as state laments over Tamil Nadu's restriction
primary_source.content: Thiruvananthapuram: While Keralam suffers acute shortage of construction materials owing to the restriction imposed by Tamil Nadu government in transporting construction materials, huge quantities of construction materials are remaining unutilised in the rivers and dams in the state. According to a data presented by the state government in the assembly, after the 2018-19 floods it was evaluated that 43 of the 44 rivers in Keralam alone had a sand and silt deposit of&nbsp; 30.17 million cubic metre that could be removed. The capacity of 15 of the 81 dams in the state alone came down by an average of 13.8 percent owing to the silt accumulation. Huge sand deposits in Kerala rivers remain untapped Studies have found that the carrying capacity of Vebanad lake, the largest lake in Keralam, came down by up to 85 percent owing to reasons like silt deposit as well as encroachments. The silt accumulation in the water bodies, which reduced the water holding capacity, has been found to be a reason for flash floods in the state. Keralam, which requires up to 30 million metric tonnes of sand annually, has been highly dependent on Tamil Nadu for rocks to sand. Hence the restriction by the neighbouring state has led to an acute scarcity in Keralam, which already led to almost three times cost escalation. Major infrastructure projects like the ongoing expansion of Vizhinjam international seaport and national highway were reportedly feeling the heat. Desilting of the water bodies is hence considered to have multiple benefits ranging from addressing construction material shortage to flood mitigation. Tamil Nadu bans transportation of rough stones to other states; Kerala seeks review The state government was forced to impose a ban on river sand mining in 2016 in view of the massive unregulated sand mining which even diverted the direction of flow of rivers at many places. Hence, the state has been depending on manufactured sand for construction. The stringent regulations for quarries have also&nbsp; led to the number of quarries coming down around 220 from 3800 ten years back, according to the Keralam Mining and Crushing Owners Association. Even as the state government initiated steps for desilting at a couple of dams like the Mangalam dam in Palakkad and introduced stringent norms for regulated river sand mining following the 2018-19 floods, those steps went into troubled waters&nbsp; owing to allegations of over exploitation and ecological concerns. Industry sources said that since the chances of Tamil Nadu easing the restrictions was remote, the state government should proactively take steps to address the crisis.&nbsp; Natural river sand offers a better construction quality than manufactured sand. Hence the government should take steps for regulated desilting and river sand mining," said Confederation of Real Estate Developers' Associations of India general convener general. However, environmental expert V Subashchandrabose points out that even as scientific desilting and river sand mining could be allowed, the state should popularise alternative&nbsp; construction methods that could reduce the dependence on natural resources.

sources.headline: Huge sand deposits remain utilised in Keralam even as state laments over Tamil Nadu's restriction

brief_bullets: Thiruvananthapuram: While Keralam suffers acute shortage of construction materials owing to the restriction imposed by Tamil Nadu government in transporting construction materials, huge quantities of construction materials are remaining unutilised in the rivers and dams in the state.

According to a data presented by the state government in the assembly, after the 2018-19 floods it was evaluated that 43 of the 44 rivers in Keralam alone had a sand and silt deposit of  30.17 million cubic metre that could be removed.
The capacity of 15 of the 81 dams in the state alone came down by an average of 13.8 percent owing to the silt accumulation.

Huge sand deposits in Kerala rivers remain untapped Studies have found that the carrying capacity of Vebanad lake, the largest lake in Keralam, came down by up to 85 percent owing to reasons like silt deposit as well as encroachments.
The silt accumulation in the water bodies, which reduced the water holding capacity, has been found to be a reason for flash floods in the state.

primary_source.headline: How to make the perfect poires belle Hélène – recipe | Felicity Cloake's How to make the perfect …
primary_source.content: Cool, juicy pears, cold ice-cream, hot chocolate sauce and a crunchy garnish – the perfect puddingIt’s always slightly embarrassing to realise that you’ve missed a pop culture reference, even if it’s 162 years old, so I won’t dwell on the fact that until last week I was unaware of the existence of Offenbach’s 1864 operetta about Helen of Troy, La Belle Hélène, after which today’s dish is named. In any case, the great French chef Escoffier was so moved by it, or perhaps by its popularity among Parisian diners, to name this simple dessert of vanilla-scented poached pears topped with hot chocolate sauce after the work’s heroine, played by the comely Hortense Schneider.Though other homages (he includes no fewer than five dishes with that name in his 1907 Guide Culinaire, none of which involve pears) may, like the music, have faded from public consciousness, this particular pairing, if you’ll forgive the pun, has stood the test of time. As Nigel Slater observes in Tender: Volume 2, “The marriage of pears and chocolate is extraordinary. It is as if they were made for each other.” This, I think, is the duo at its “most sumptuous”. stories.primary_headline: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings

primary_source.headline: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings
primary_source.content: Anthropic argues that its own workplace trends could be indicators of “how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy,” especially since the company “has thoroughly molded its workflows around AI.” But even if other organizations never embrace AI as thoroughly or in the exact same way as Anthropic, the report offers an intriguing glimpse at how the company currently operates. Notably, Anthropic is making fewer junior hires, with the proportion of junior-level employees in technical departments falling from 21% to 14% since early 2025, and the proportion of junior technical hires falling even more sharply, from 27% to 9%. Anthropic also says that technical teams now represent a smaller share of the overall workforce, falling from 61% to 56% — a trend that it attributes to  “natural expansion of business functions as the company scales,” as well as “coding tools increasingly allowing non-technical employees to make software themselves.” One employee reportedly described an “eternal pressure at Anthropic to move as fast as possible and use Claude for everything.” In an April 2026 survey, 27% of employees said they had become more productive because of Claude  and 20% said their job had shifted “from actually doing work to managing Claudes”; apparently one engineered compared this to babysitting: “When you are babysitting, every child brings to you concerns with an equal demand for your attention and the various [Claudes] also do that.” In fact, the report suggests “human attention and judgement” are becoming a “bottleneck” for productivity, as Claude produces a “deluge” of text that needs to be read and organized. Unsurprisingly, the report argues that AI adoption has made the company more productive, as indicated by “more code per person, closing more sales per rep, and processing more contracts.” The company acknowledges that “more code does not necessarily mean better code or business impact,” but it also hasn’t found any indications that code quality is declining.

stories.primary_headline: Karnataka BJP chief Vijayendra’s meeting with ex-party MLA Yatnal sets political tongues wagging

primary_source.headline: Karnataka BJP chief Vijayendra’s meeting with ex-party MLA Yatnal sets political tongues wagging
primary_source.content: Dharwad: A meeting between BJP State president B Y Vijayendra and expelled party MLA Basangouda Patil Yatnal at a private function has set tongues wagging in political circles, fuelling speculation about the latter’s possible return to the party.Vijayendra was in Hubballi campaigning for BJP candidate S V Sankanur, who is contesting the West Graduates’ Constituency election to the Legislative Council. After the campaign, he attended a religious programme at Varur, near Hubballi, where Yatnal was also present.Following the programme, the two leaders visited the residence of a prominent journalist in Chebbi village. Yatnal arrived first, followed by Vijayendra.Karnataka Council polls: Expelled leader Basanagouda Patil Yatnal pledges support to BJPWhile BJP workers expected Yatnal to leave after Vijayendra’s arrival, the two leaders exchanged pleasantries and held a conversation lasting nearly 30 minutes, taking many by surprise.The interaction has triggered speculation within political circles about the possibility of Yatnal returning to the BJP fold, potentially signalling a thaw in the strained relationship between the two leaders.A senior BJP functionary described the meeting as a positive development, saying the party would welcome Yatnal’s return if differences could be resolved.“The party wants everyone to set aside past bitterness and work together to strengthen the organisation ahead of the next Assembly election,” the functionary said.However, it remains to be seen whether the meeting marks the beginning of a rapprochement within the State BJP or was merely a courtesy call at a private gathering.

stories.primary_headline: There are five signs that someone dislikes you – but it’s best to ignore them | Polly Hudson

primary_source.headline: There are five signs that someone dislikes you – but it’s best to ignore them | Polly Hudson
primary_source.content: All the possible indications, from eye contact to body language, come with a disclaimer. The truth is, you can never be totally sure ...I’d be far less paranoid if everyone wasn’t out to get me, so when BBC Science Focus dangled “The subtle signs somebody secretly dislikes you”, I’ve never clicked so fast. Knowledge is power, after all, and the promised signals came courtesy of psychologists via a magazine with the word science in its title.The first indication? They avoid eye contact. Apparently “someone who repeatedly looks away, scans the room or avoids mutual gaze might be creating psychological distance”. Agreed. But they may also be checking to see who else arrives, which might not mean they secretly hate you, only that they secretly don’t like you as much as whoever just came in. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: 'Couldn't prevent regime change within Shiv Sena': Maharashtra CM Fadnavis takes dig at Uddhav Thackeray

primary_source.headline: 'Couldn't prevent regime change within Shiv Sena': Maharashtra CM Fadnavis takes dig at Uddhav Thackeray
primary_source.content: Mumbai: A day after Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray backed the ‘regime change’ call, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Sunday took a dig at him saying he could not prevent a regime change in his own party. Fadnavis was referring to the June-July 2022 rebellion in the Shiv Sena led by Eknath Shinde — who toppled Thackeray’s Maha Vikas Aghadi government with the help of BJP to become the Chief Minister. Slamming Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Thackeray on Saturday said: “Yes we are ready for a regime change…particularly If right to express ourselves through vote and right to protest is being taken away then we have to change regime.”Uddhav Thackeray backs Prashant Bhushan's regime change call, cites curbs on voting, protest rightsHowever, Fadnavis, on Sunday hit back at Thackeray, a former ally, who is now a key leader of the Congress-led INDIA opposition bloc. "Firstly, if Uddhav Thackeray could not prevent a 'regime change' within the Shiv Sena itself, I fail to understand what other 'regime change' he is referring to,” said Fadnavis, a senior BJP leader. "When his party abandoned Hindutva and discarded the ideals of the ‘Hindu Hriday Samrat' and Shiv Sena supremo Balasaheb Thackeray, it caused such an upheaval within his own ranks that those who wished to remain true to Balasaheb’s vision formed the 'real' Shiv Sena,” said Fadnavis. “My clear message is — stop challenging the Constitution of India. Decisions here will be made in Parliament, in accordance with the Constitution—not on the streets,” he said, adding: “If you want a regime change, you have to contest polls, win the hearts of the people, and secure a mandate.”

stories.primary_headline: Wikipedia often gets taken for granted – but its history is fascinating, and its future is fragile

primary_source.headline: Wikipedia often gets taken for granted – but its history is fascinating, and its future is fragile
primary_source.content: Wikipedia’s 68m articles have been consulted trillions of times. Not bad for a website that has barely changed since it was founded 20 years agoA few years ago, I was struck by the tension between how Wikipedia was used, and how it was talked about. Everyone was on it all the time, and yet its reputation had stalled at “don’t trust it”, because it was the “free encyclopedia that anyone can edit”.Clearly people were trusting it, so much so it had become part of the fabric of everyday life since it was founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger in 2001. But despite the fact it now has been consulted trillions of times by billions of people (English Wikipedia alone is 5.2bn words long), it inspires an odd lack of curiosity. Even people donating to Wikipedia might say the money was “for the factcheckers”, though there aren’t any – not paid ones, anyway. Meanwhile, the internet in the social media era had begun to feel like a much uglier place, and some digital nostalgia was setting in: here was this holdover that had somehow survived; a website that functions – and even looks – much the same as it did 20 years ago. stories.primary_headline: ‘This is horrifying. This is madness’: the row over competitive yoga

primary_source.headline: ‘This is horrifying. This is madness’: the row over competitive yoga
primary_source.content: Some yogis welcome the idea of competition – for others, it is anathema. Will those keen for yoga to become an Olympic sport win the argument?Vaishnavi Saravanakumar describes herself on Instagram as “India’s rubber band girl”. In a typical video post, dressed in a rhinestone-studded crimson catsuit and accompanied by a Bollywood-rap anthem, she demonstrates an improbable feat. From standing, she snakes into a deep back bend, curls her head and shoulders up under her tiger-striped calves, and finishes beaming to camera with ankles crossed under her chin. This is yoga as we have seldom seen it before.Earlier this year, the Indian government announced that it will push for yogasana’s inclusion in the Olympics, ahead of the country’s bid to host the 2036 Games. The news came the week before the inaugural World Yogasana Championship, held in Ahmedabad in June, at which Saravanakumar, a gold medallist, was one of 522 yogis competing. Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: BJP's Yediyurappa alleges CM Shivakumar part of plot to dethrone Siddaramaiah
primary_source.content: Davanagere: BJP Parliamentary Board member and former Chief Minister B S Yediyurappa charged that many leaders including Chief Minister D K Shivakumar hatched a conspiracy to dethrone Siddaramaiah from the post of chief minister.Addressing media persons, here on Sunday, he stated that tolerance of Siddaramaiah is difficult to understand, but noted that the truth will soon come to light. He remarked that a systematic plot was executed to remove Siddaramaiah from the top post and create chaos in the state. D K Shivakumar is intoxicated by power and shows no willingness to correct his mistakes.HDK, JD(S) workers stage protest outside DGP office, demand immediate arrest of Rakesh Shetty over 'sting op' videosResponding to a question, he said, the state government is oblivious to the drought situation and the hardships faced by the people and farmers. The people must teach them a fitting lesson in the next election.Meanwhile, Chitradurga MP Govind Karjol urged that those in politics should serve as role models for society rather than acting like 'demons.' He called for an end to such low-level politics and demanded strict legal action against those who engage in despicable acts like 'sting operations.'

stories.primary_headline: ‘Medieval romance overflowed with sexually active fairies’: the surprisingly long roots of romantasy

primary_source.headline: ‘Medieval romance overflowed with sexually active fairies’: the surprisingly long roots of romantasy
primary_source.content: Critics mock it as raunchy trash – but this enchanting genre is much older, and wilder, than you might imagineThere’s a popular genre, filled with beautiful, human-sized fairies having sex with humans (often quite violent sex, but the people reading it seem to enjoy it). Word is that it’s badly written and unashamedly escapist – all golden, glittering palaces, wild adventure and, of course, gorgeous fairies. It’s certainly popular – plenty of the stories have been translated into numerous languages, spreading across continents. Serious commentators are sure it spells bad news: at best, it’s just a load of trash; at worst, it’s actively leading people astray. Most damningly of all, women produce and consume it. Welcome to the 12th century, where fairy romance is all the rage. Sound familiar?The romantasy that fills our shelves and bestseller lists – from Sarah J Maas’s A Court of Thorns and Roses to Callie Hart’s Quicksilver – is not a new genre, but part of a centuries-old heritage. You only need to look at the medieval predecessors of the modern romantasy novel to understand why it’s enjoyed by millions and why, even after hundreds of years, fairy romance has such power over us – and why there are still those who want to diminish and dismiss it. Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: Getaway cars, affairs, Dubai fugitives: Trump’s pick Ken Paxton brings baggage to Senate race in Texas
primary_source.content: The Republican state attorney general appears uniquely ill-chosen as a candidate – but he is a political survivor who could yet frustrate Democratic dreamsDepending how you look at the situation, it is either predictable that Ken Paxton, Texas’s attorney general and Republican candidate for US Senate, is struggling in the polls – or impressive that he is not doing worse. Beloved by hardcore Maga voters and regarded with skepticism by the broader voting public, Paxton is also puzzlingly bland. Recently, Donald Trump told a crowd of supporters that the 63-year-old Paxton “may not dress right, he may not talk exactly perfectly, and he may not be the best-looking guy I’ve ever seen”. The president was endorsing him.Yet it is Paxton’s ability to attract – and somehow scrape through – scandal that makes him a less charismatic, perhaps, but still kindred spirit of “Teflon Don”: nothing sticks. He has survived state prosecution (on securities-related charges that he settled without admitting guilt), impeachment by the Republican-led Texas legislature (on abuse-of-office charges of which he was later acquitted), and so many controversies that it can be difficult to pin down the most outrageous. brief_bullets: The Republican state attorney general appears uniquely ill-chosen as a candidate – but he is a political survivor who could yet frustrate Democratic dreamsDepending how you look at the situation, it is either predictable that Ken Paxton, Texas’s attorney general and Republican candidate for US Senate, is struggling in the polls – or impressive that he is not doing worse.
Beloved by hardcore Maga voters and regarded with skepticism by the broader voting public, Paxton is also puzzlingly bland.
Recently, Donald Trump told a crowd of supporters that the 63-year-old Paxton “may not dress right, he may not talk exactly perfectly, and he may not be the best-looking guy I’ve ever seen”.

The president was endorsing him.Yet it is Paxton’s ability to attract – and somehow scrape through – scandal that makes him a less charismatic, perhaps, but still kindred spirit of “Teflon Don”: nothing sticks.

He has survived state prosecution (on securities-related charges that he settled without admitting guilt), impeachment by the Republican-led Texas legislature (on abuse-of-office charges of which he was later acquitted), and so many controversies that it can be difficult to pin down the most outrageous.

stories.primary_headline: ‘Shakespeare was a Black woman’: the playwright’s under-recognized connection to Black culture

primary_source.headline: ‘Shakespeare was a Black woman’: the playwright’s under-recognized connection to Black culture
primary_source.content: A new Washington DC exhibition examines how Toni Morrison, Maya Angelou and more used the Bard’s work to help tell their own stories“William Shakespeare was a black woman.” In 1985, Maya Angelou spoke these words as part of a keynote speech at a convention in Cedar Rapids, Iowa.There, she spoke of the role poetry played in her transition from muteness as a child and how she fantasized herself triumphantly delivering Portia’s speech from William Shakespeare’s The Merchant of Venice in front of her entire community at church. Though she never got the chance to perform that rendition, Angelou acknowledged her desire to deliver that rendition as part of a lifelong kinship with Shakespeare, a connection she continued to seek out throughout her life whenever she needed heartening or solace. In her eyes, Shakespeare wrote his emotionally desolate Sonnet 29 “for” her; how else could he have so aptly described the harsh realities of the Black feminine condition? Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: ‘I suffer a lot’: Villarreal owner Fernando Roig on not enjoying games and the prospect of Liverpool | Sid Lowe

In Kalkan, it still feels like summer; the harbourfront restaurants throng with visitors, the day gulets (wooden boats) still putter in and out of the bay and you don’t have to wait an hour to get a taxi back to your villa. primary_source.headline: ‘How do we welcome the stranger, with humanity or anger?’ The forgotten Germans who found refuge in Ireland
primary_source.content: A new play revisits the story of Ireland’s 18th-century German refugees, whose experience of prejudice and exclusion resonates with today’s debates over immigrationIn the early 18th century, a few thousand Germans fled religious persecution and near starvation in their homeland and ended up in remote rural Irish villages. The Irish Palatines, as they were known, were poor, conservative homesteaders who couldn’t speak the language and were the object of suspicion and violence – precursors to the displaced Syrians or Afghans of the past decade.Their story is told in Refuge, a co-production between Staatstheater Mainz and the Irish company Fishamble.
